title: Numerical Solution of Equations Module 2 Lesson 1: Rearrange to a Valid Iteration custom practice

evidence_basis.originality_note: All prompts, values and combinations are original; mapped Cambridge evidence informs scope and assessment structure only.

parts.prompt: Show that the equation $x^3 - 3x - 5 = 0$ can be rearranged into the form $x = \sqrt{3 + \dfrac{5}{x}}$ for $x > 0$.
Show that the equation $x^3 = \mathrm{e}^{2x - 1}$, where $x > 0$, can be rearranged into the iterative formula $x_{n+1} = \dfrac{1}{2}(3\ln x_n + 1)$.
Show that the equation $x\tan x = 3$ can be rearranged into the iterative formula $x_{n+1} = \tan^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{3}{x_n}\right)$ for $0 < x < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.
Show that if the iterative sequence given by $x_{n+1} = \dfrac{2x_n^3 + 7}{3x_n^2 - 1}$ converges to a limit $\alpha$, then $\alpha$ is a root of the equation $x^3 - x - 7 = 0$.

The equation $x^3 + 2x - 5 = 0$ has a root $\alpha$ close to $1.33$. Consider the rearrangement $x = F(x)$ where $F(x) = (5 - 2x)^{1/3}$. By finding $F'(x)$ and evaluating $|F'(1.33)|$, explain why the iteration $x_{n+1} = (5 - 2x_n)^{1/3}$ converges to $\alpha$.

The diagram illustrates the first three steps of the fixed-point iteration $x_{n+1} = F(x_n)$ starting from $x_0 = 1.6$, where $y = F(x)$ has gradient $F'(\alpha) = -0.4$ at the intersection $(2, 2)$ with $y = x$.

State whether the diagram represents a staircase or cobweb pattern, and explain why the sequence converges to the root $\alpha = 2$.

figure.purpose: Provide visual cobweb iteration context on y = x and y = F(x) to test graphical interpretation of convergence and oscillation.
figure.alt_text: Cobweb iteration diagram showing y = x and y = F(x) with negative gradient -0.4 intersecting at (2, 2), spiraling inward towards the root.
figure.brief: Draw Cartesian axes with line y = x and curve y = F(x) intersecting at (2, 2) with slope -0.4. Show vertical and horizontal line segments starting from x_0 = 1.6 on the x-axis, going vertically to y = F(x_0), horizontally to y = x, vertically to y = F(x_1), horizontally to y = x, illustrating a cobweb spiraling inwards toward (2, 2).

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the equation $2x^3 - 7x + 3 = 0$ can be rearranged into the form $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{7x - 3}{2x}}$ for $x > \dfrac{3}{7}$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Show that the equation $2x^3 - 7x + 3 = 0$ can also be rearranged into the alternative iterative form $x_{n+1} = \dfrac{2x_n^3 + 3}{7}$.

questions.prompt: The equation $\mathrm{e}^{2x} - 4x - 5 = 0$ has a single positive root $\alpha$ in the interval $1.1 < x < 1.3$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the equation $\mathrm{e}^{2x} - 4x - 5 = 0$ can be rearranged into the form $x = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(4x + 5)$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Let $F(x) = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(4x + 5)$. Find $F'(x)$ and, by evaluating $F'(x)$ at $x = 1.2$, explain why the iteration $x_{n+1} = \dfrac{1}{2}\ln(4x_n + 5)$ is guaranteed to converge to $\alpha$.

questions.prompt: The equation $x\sin x = 1$ has a single root $\alpha$ in the interval $\dfrac{\pi}{6} < x < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, with $\alpha \approx 1.114$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the equation $x\sin x = 1$ can be rearranged into the iterative formula $x_{n+1} = \operatorname{cosec} x_n$ for $\dfrac{\pi}{6} < x < \dfrac{\pi}{2}$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
A student suggests using the alternative rearrangement $x_{n+1} = \sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{x_n}\right)$. Let $F(x) = \sin^{-1}\!\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right)$.

(i) Show that $F'(x) = -\dfrac{1}{x\sqrt{x^2 - 1}}$ for $x > 1$.
(ii) By evaluating $|F'(1.114)|$, explain why this iteration fails to converge to $\alpha$.

questions.prompt: The diagram shows part of the line $y = x$ and the curve $y = F(x)$, where $F(x) = \sqrt{\dfrac{x + 6}{2}}$. The curve intersects the line at the point $(\alpha, \alpha)$, corresponding to the positive root of $2x^2 - x - 6 = 0$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the equation $2x^2 - x - 6 = 0$ can be rearranged into the form $x = \sqrt{\dfrac{x + 6}{2}}$ for $x > 0$, and find the exact value of the positive root $\alpha$ by factorising the quadratic equation.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt:
(i) Find $F'(x)$ and evaluate $F'(\alpha)$ at $\alpha = 2$.
(ii) Explain why the iteration $x_{n+1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{x_n + 6}{2}}$ produces a staircase pattern rather than a cobweb pattern, and confirm that the sequence converges to $2$.

figure.purpose: Provide visual staircase iteration context on y = x and y = F(x) to test graphical interpretation of monotonic convergence.
figure.alt_text: Staircase iteration diagram showing y = x and y = sqrt((x+6)/2) intersecting at (2, 2), with stepped iteration path starting at x0 = 1 approaching (2, 2).
figure.brief: Draw Cartesian axes with line y = x and curve y = sqrt((x+6)/2) intersecting at (2, 2). Starting at x0 = 1 on the x-axis, draw vertical line to y = F(x0) = sqrt(3.5) approx 1.87, horizontal line to y = x at (1.87, 1.87), vertical line to y = F(1.87) approx 1.98, forming a monotonic staircase stepping towards (2, 2).

questions.prompt: The cubic equation $x^3 + 3x - 1 = 0$ has a single real root $\alpha$ in the interval $0.3 < x < 0.4$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the equation $x^3 + 3x - 1 = 0$ can be rearranged into the iterative formula $x_{n+1} = \dfrac{1 - x_n^3}{3}$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: A student proposes the alternative iterative formula $x_{n+1} = (1 - 3x_n)^{1/3}$. Let $G(x) = (1 - 3x)^{1/3}$. By finding $G'(x)$ and evaluating $|G'(0.32)|$, explain why this alternative iteration fails to find $\alpha$.

questions.prompt: The transcendental equation $x^2 \mathrm{e}^x = 8$ has a positive root $\alpha$ in the interval $1.2 < x < 1.4$, with $\alpha \approx 1.34$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Show that the equation $x^2 \mathrm{e}^x = 8$ can be rearranged into the iterative formula $x_{n+1} = \ln\!\left(\dfrac{8}{x_n^2}\right)$ for $x > 0$, and also into the alternative iterative formula $x_{n+1} = \sqrt{8\mathrm{e}^{-x_n}}$.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Let $F(x) = \ln 8 - 2\ln x$ and $G(x) = \sqrt{8}\,\mathrm{e}^{-x/2}$. By finding $F'(1.34)$ and $G'(1.34)$, determine which of the two iterative formulas converges to $\alpha$, fully justifying your choice.

questions.prompt: The cubic equation $x^3 - 5x + 1 = 0$ has three distinct real roots: $\alpha_1 \approx -2.33$, $\alpha_2 \approx 0.20$, and $\alpha_3 \approx 2.13$.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt:
Consider the rearrangement $x = F(x) = \dfrac{x^3 + 1}{5}$.

(i) Find $F'(x)$.
(ii) By evaluating $F'(x)$ at each of the three roots, determine which of the three roots the iteration $x_{n+1} = \dfrac{x_n^3 + 1}{5}$ is capable of converging to.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: To locate the largest root $\alpha_3 \approx 2.13$, a student uses the rearrangement $x = H(x) = (5x - 1)^{1/3}$. By finding $H'(\alpha_3)$, prove that the iteration $x_{n+1} = (5x_n - 1)^{1/3}$ converges to $\alpha_3$.
